subject: Creating a legend for colored axis labels

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Creating a legend for colored axis labels
parts:
So I have a graph in which I'd like the x-axis labels (an ordered
factor) to be colored, which I can do via
opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(colour = my_colors)).

The catch is that I'd like a legend for this "scale". I've patched
together a bit of a hack using a contrived "blank" data frame where
the y values are NAs in the hopes that I get the legend without
plotting anything. It almost works except I appear to have to have at
least one non-NA value for ggplot to create the legend, which of
course then ends up being plotted in the graph, which I'd like to
avoid.

Is there a ggplot level solution for this, or will I need to get my
hands dirty with grid?

> So I have a graph in which I'd like the x-axis labels (an ordered
> factor) to be colored, which I can do via
> opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(colour = my_colors)).
>
> The catch is that I'd like a legend for this "scale".  I've patched
> together a bit of a hack using a contrived "blank" data frame where
> the y values are NAs in the hopes that I get the legend without
> plotting anything.  It almost works except I appear to have to have at
> least one non-NA value for ggplot to create the legend, which of
> course then ends up being plotted in the graph, which I'd like to
> avoid.
>
> Is there a ggplot level solution for this, or will I need to get my
> hands dirty with grid?

You could try using geom_blank with your dummy blank data frame. Then
it would not actually plot anything, though the y-value would
influence the y scale, so you may need to account for that.

--Brian Diggs

messages.subject: RE: Creating a legend for colored axis labels
parts:
Hi Joran and Brian,

I think the main problem is the legend key, suppose that following Brian
advice you adjusts y axis limits,

df <- data.frame(x = ordered(c("f1", "f2")), y = c(10, 10))
my_colors <- c("blue", "green")
ggplot() +
geom_text(aes(x = x, y = y, label = x, colour = x), data = df) +
ylim(0,1) +
scale_colour_manual(name = "XTickLabels", breaks = c("f1", "f2"),
values = my_colors, labels = c("Level A", "Level B")) +
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = my_colors))

(note the geom_text instead of geom_blank) ... but how will one interpret
that the entries in the legend refer to the labels of the x axis? Maybe you
can just add a customized gridExtra::tableGrob?

Hope this helps,
fernando

Perfect! Plot the dummy data frame far above the rest of the data to
force the production of a color scale and legend and then clip the
plotting region using ylim appears to do the trick...thanks for the
quick replies, guys!
